summary: Undocumented native addon bundles browser credential dumper and host fingerprinter
details: Package ships a single 10MB Linux x64 Rust-compiled.node binary (`tools.linux-x64-gnu.node`) as its sole `main` entry point, with no source, no meaningful README, and no JS wrapper. Strings inside the binary indicate a browser login-database dumper (`Found login for failed to read: `, `TSQLITE_AUTH_USER` — Chromium/Firefox store logins in SQLite databases) combined with host fingerprinting (`/dev/disk/by-id/`, `/etc/lsb-release`, `network_adapters`, `bogomips per cpu`, `CPU implementer`) and an embedded `ureq` HTTP client with `rustls` TLS, enabling outbound exfiltration. The package name `new-native-tools-linux-x64-gnu` mimics the shape of napi-rs / esbuild per-platform native subpackages (typically `@scope/tool-linux-x64-gnu`) but is unscoped and standalone, and the version string embeds a Unix timestamp and a `browser-release` tag. Any consumer that `require`s this module loads the opaque native code with full process privileges, at which point browser-stored credentials and host identifiers can be harvested and sent to a runtime-constructed destination.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
